set.body:
Regressor.fromEvents filters events with amplitude == 0.0:

    val filtered = events.iterator.filter(_.amplitude != 0.0).toVector

Three events in, two retained. For HrfAssignment.PerEvent the surviving HRFs are re-indexed to match.

This is defensible as an optimization for a plain condition regressor, but it silently breaks the correspondence between input event i and output event i, which is exactly what trial-wise models rely on. LSA and LSS address trials by index; a zero-amplitude trial vanishing shifts every subsequent one.

Options:
- keep the filter but make it explicit in the returned type (retained indices, or an error when PerEvent HRFs are supplied)
- drop the filter and let the zero amplitude do its own work (it contributes nothing anyway; the only cost is a wasted convolution)

Second option is probably right: the optimization saves little and the invariant is worth more.

Verified present: modules/hrf/.../regressor/Regressor.scala fromEvents. Context: docs/plans/hrf-hardening.md section 3.7.
set.title: Regressor silently drops zero-amplitude events, breaking per-event index correspondence
